question.problem: Find the set of values of $x$ that satisfy $2<2x+4\le 6$ and $4x>12.$
question.worked_solution:
To solve compound "and" inequalities, we solve each inequality separately and then find their intersection.

- First, we solve $2<2x+4\le 6\,:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & <2x+4\le 6 \\ 2-4 & <2x+4-4\le 6-4 \\ -2 & <2x\le 2 \\ \frac{-2}{2} & <\frac{2x}{2}\le \frac{2}{2} \\ -1 & <x\le 1\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14224662/assets/485e77fe84f5745120d5f450c3e1043ee61463a83f7c12bfc6d1ae0e4124a38b.png)

   

- Then, we solve  $4x>12\,:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4x & >12 \\ \frac{4x}{4} & >\frac{12}{4} \\ x & >3\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14224662/assets/654f97a64ec1a13b4a94860dfa07d05f7c119a5fe2084ba23aa994a97f0bea70.png)

To find the values of $x$ that satisfy both inequalities, we find where the two solutions overlap:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14224662/assets/d2d0f41792356b6c250612b033413f66bfd7a35440e1b84da660fccd5c1285b0.png)

$$

$$

It turns out that the solutions do not overlap at all. Therefore, there are no values of $x$ that satisfy both inequalities simultaneously. So, there is no solution.
